title: The Matrix
logline: A sleep-deprived hacker haunted by 'What is the Matrix?' is hunted by unkillable Agents and offered a red pill that reveals his world is a neural simulation farming humans; to prove he is more than code he must re-enter the system to rescue the man who believes he is the One.
premise: Thomas A. Anderson, hacker 'Neo,' lives a double life between Meta CorTechs drudgery and nights hunting the question 'What is the Matrix?' (ev-004 sc-012). Contacted through his own PC and led by Trinity's white rabbit pin (ev-004 sc-013), he is seized by Agents Smith, Brown and Jones who offer to wipe his record for Morpheus then seal his mouth and implant a wire-tap bug (ev-007 sc-020). Given a final choice between forgetting and knowing, he swallows the red pill (ev-010 sc-028-030), his mirror liquefies into him, and he is torn from a magenta amnion pod via the coaxial jack at his skull and flushed into the waste pipes before the hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar recovers him into the scorched real world of 2197 (ev-011 sc-031-034). Told humans are batteries grown in fields after scorching the sky (ev-013 sc-039) and that Zion near the earth's core is humanity's last city (ev-013), he fails every test of belief — beaten in the dojo (ev-015 sc-056) and falling short on the rooftop jump (ev-016 sc-058) — is told by the Oracle he is not the One and must choose between his life and Morpheus's (ev-023 sc-085), watches Cypher murder Apoc and Switch for a steak-deal to be reinserted rich (ev-020 sc-074, ev-029 sc-137), then denies he is the One and still re-enters the Matrix to pull Morpheus from the government building (ev-032 sc-148, ev-034 sc-165), dies from three point-blank shots in hall 303 (ev-043 sc-205), and is revived by Trinity's kiss to halt bullets and destroy Smith from inside (ev-044 sc-209, ev-045 sc-216-218).
setting: Dual-layered reality: a neural-interactive simulation of America at the end of the Twentieth Century — Heart O' The City Hotel Room 303, Meta CorTechs offices, Hotel Lafayette and a downtown government building — overlaying the scorched real world circa 2197 of sewer mains, towers of magenta amnion pods, and the hovercraft Nebuchadnezzar en route to Zion deep underground near the earth's core (ev-011 sc-031, ev-013 sc-039, ev-019 sc-066).
pov: Third-person limited anchored to Neo/Thomas A. Anderson, with objective cutaways to Trinity, Morpheus, Cypher and Agent Smith
style: Tech-noir and Hong Kong wire-fu hybrid: green code rain and Construct loading, mirrored surfaces that liquefy and crawl (ev-010 sc-030), frozen-time Agent reveals on a crowded street (ev-018 sc-065), and long philosophical interrogations intercut with brutal, physics-bending set-pieces where belief dictates whether gravity bends or breaks (ev-015 sc-048-056, ev-016 sc-058).

narrative_vector.goal: Neo wants to answer the obsessive splinter 'What is the Matrix?' and, after learning the answer, to rescue Morpheus and prove he can become the One he denies he is (ev-004 sc-012, ev-032 sc-148).
narrative_vector.motivation: A lifelong dread that the world is false — 'you hardly sleep... you sit at your computer' hunting the Matrix (ev-004) — and later faith in Morpheus and Trinity after they risk everything to free him from the pod (ev-011 sc-033, ev-044 sc-211).
narrative_vector.conflict: The system itself resists: Agents Smith, Brown and Jones who can possess any hardwired person and have killed everyone who fought them (ev-018 sc-065), Sentinels hunting the ship's electromagnetic wake (ev-019 sc-066), Cypher's betrayal from within (ev-029 sc-137), and Neo's own disbelief that makes the mind make death real (ev-013 sc-039).
narrative_vector.generative_question: Will Neo stop running from the Agents and choose to die for another man, thereby rewriting the rule that death in the Matrix is final and becoming the One?

audiences.why_this_group: They engage because the film literalizes Baudrillard's Simulacra hidden as hollowed disks (ev-004 sc-012) and stages the Oracle's 'Know Thyself' prophecy versus choice (ev-014 sc-045, ev-023 sc-085) as a testable system, not a metaphor.
audiences.reader_promise: You will get a rigorous what-if where every miracle is a rule-bend explained in the dojo (ev-015 sc-056) and rooftop jump (ev-016 sc-058) and paid off when Neo stops bullets by reading code (ev-045 sc-216).

audiences.why_this_group: They come for kinetic, physics-bending combat that is system-legal: Trinity's impossible rooftop escape duplicated by Agent Brown (ev-003 sc-005-011) and the lobby-to-helicopter assault on the government building (ev-033 sc-155, ev-034 sc-165).
audiences.reader_promise: You will get escalating set-pieces where each fight raises the cost — from Morpheus beating Neo to the floor (ev-015 sc-056) to the subway train kill-box where Smith chokes Neo by the third rail (ev-039 sc-182) to Neo bursting out of Smith (ev-045 sc-218).

rules_of_the_world: Exit from the Matrix requires a hardwired ringing phone; Trinity must run for the Wells and Lake payphone (ev-003 sc-005), the crew smashes into the wet-wall to reach Room 808's phone (ev-024 sc-105-114), and Neo's final escape is a dive for a ringing hall phone as Sentinels overrun the ship (ev-046 sc-219-222).

Death in the Matrix kills the real body because 'the mind makes it real' and 'the body cannot live without the mind' (ev-013 sc-039); Mouse stays dead in Room 1313 (ev-023 sc-085-104) and Neo flatlines after three chest shots in hall 303 (ev-044 sc-209).

Agents are sentient programs who can move in and out of any person still hardwired to the system (ev-018 sc-065); Smith reveals himself from the drunk in the subway booth (ev-037 sc-176) and Brown matches Trinity's 40-foot rooftop jump (ev-003 sc-005-011).

Physical laws are system rules: 'Some can be bent. Others can be broken' only if the mind is freed (ev-013 sc-039); Morpheus proves it by crossing the rooftop gap (ev-016 sc-058) while Neo falls short until belief shifts and he later halts bullets (ev-045 sc-216).

Humans are grown in magenta amnion-filled pods with a coaxial jack locked into the base of the skull, stacked in towers after humans scorched the sky to deny machines solar power (ev-011 sc-031, ev-013 sc-039); Zion survives deep underground near the earth's core and the crew's only weapon against Sentinels is an EMP that disables electrical systems but cannot fire while anyone is jacked in (ev-019 sc-066, ev-044 sc-209).

The machines run a trace program that fixes a jacked-in signal; it captures Trinity's call at #312-555 (ev-002 sc-004) and the deja-vu cat signals the Matrix was rewritten into a trap that cuts the hardline (ev-023 sc-085-104).
forbidden_tics: No omniscient voiceover exposition; truth is shown via Construct loading and Morpheus walking Neo through the desert of the real (ev-013 sc-039-044) rather than narrated.

No invulnerable hero; Neo is dismantled in the dojo (ev-015 sc-056), falls badly short on the jump and spits blood into his hand (ev-016 sc-058-061), and is confirmed dead by Agent Brown before revival (ev-044 sc-209).

No magic without system cost; every bend risks death and the EMP cannot be triggered while the crew is jacked in, forcing Morpheus to wait at the switch as Sentinels descend (ev-019 sc-066, ev-046 sc-219).

No quippy meta-humor or fourth-wall winks; Agents remain cold system enforcers and Smith's disgust at the collective hunt — 'withdraws from the unit in disgust, insisting the quarry is not gone' (ev-036 sc-174) — is played straight.

identification_value.admirable_strength: Neo's admirable strength is relentless truth-seeking that hardens into faith-driven courage — the audience wants his willingness to choose a painful reality over a comfortable lie. It is tested when he follows the white rabbit pin to Trinity's club against his plan to work the next day (ev-004 sc-013), costing sleep and safety; when he swallows the red pill after Morpheus warns 'You take the blue pill [...]' (ev-010 sc-028-030), costing his entire body as the cracked mirror liquefies into him and he is severed from the coaxial cable and flushed through waste pipes (ev-011 sc-031-033); and when he denies he is the One yet still says 'I'm going in. I believe I can bring him back' to rescue Morpheus (ev-032 sc-148-152), walking into a government building where everyone who has fought an Agent has died (ev-018 sc-065).
identification_value.opening_vulnerability: Neo's opening vulnerability is the recognisable numbness of the precarious office drone — the everyman who knows his life is hollow but complies to keep the job, mirroring the viewer's own alarm-clock dread and fear of looking foolish. The script stages it when the alarm drags him awake at 9:15 A.M. and he curses the clock-face (ev-005 sc-014), then when Rhineheart lectures him about lateness and authority and delivers an either-or ultimatum to which Neo replies with flat, deferential compliance (ev-005 sc-015-016); later, guided turn-by-turn by Morpheus's phone, he reaches the skyscraper ledge and cannot bring himself to cross, frozen while the window closes (ev-006 sc-017-019), and he recoils from the crew's touch when told humans are farmed, his body rejecting the truth (ev-013 sc-039-044).
identification_value.connection: The two halves are one mechanism: Neo's truth-hunger is the price of his alienation. Because he 'hardly sleeps... you sit at your computer' hunting the Matrix (ev-004 sc-012), he is already late, exhausted and deferential at Meta CorTechs (ev-005 sc-014-016) — the vulnerability is the daily cost of the virtue. Conversely that same virtue costs him everything when tested: swallowing the red pill (ev-010 sc-030) immediately triggers replication, cardiac arrest and the machine severing the coaxial cable at the base of his skull (ev-011 sc-031-033), and choosing to rescue Morpheus while denying he is the One (ev-032 sc-148) forces him through Smith choking him by the electrified third-rail (ev-039 sc-182) and three point-blank shots in hall 303 (ev-043 sc-205-208) before Trinity's kiss can restart his monitors (ev-044 sc-211). Strength and wound are the same splinter.

entity_roster.name: Neo / Thomas A. Anderson
entity_roster.description: A double-life programmer by day at Meta CorTechs and hacker 'Neo' by night, bald after pod extraction with a coaxial socket at the base of his skull, who is hunted as #312-555 and called 'the One' before he believes it (ev-007 sc-020, ev-011 sc-031).

entity_roster.name: Trinity
entity_roster.description: Leather-clad hacker and hovercraft crew member who initially contacts Neo through his PC, executes the 40-foot rooftop escape and window dive to the Wells and Lake phone (ev-003 sc-005-011), and later revives Neo with a kiss after flatline (ev-044 sc-211).

entity_roster.name: Morpheus
entity_roster.description: Bald captain of the Nebuchadnezzar in cracked circular mirrored glasses who offers the red/blue pill choice (ev-010 sc-028), teaches that the mind makes rules real in the dojo and on the rooftop gap (ev-015 sc-056, ev-016 sc-058), and sacrifices himself in the wall to let Trinity get Neo out (ev-025 sc-115-121).

entity_roster.name: Agent Smith
entity_roster.description: Sunglasses-wearing sentient Agent with ice-blue eyes who can possess any hardwired human, seals Neo's mouth shut and implants the fluke-worm tap (ev-007 sc-020), and later withdraws from Brown and Jones in disgust to hunt Neo personally (ev-036 sc-174).

entity_roster.name: Cypher / Mr. Reagan
entity_roster.description: Disillusioned Nebuchadnezzar crew member who pours Dozer's liquor, recasts prophecy as a body count (ev-020 sc-073), and trades Morpheus and Zion codes for a steak dinner and reinsertion as a rich actor with no memory (ev-020 sc-074, ev-029 sc-137).

entity_roster.name: Tank
entity_roster.description: Young operator who loads kung fu directly into Neo (ev-015 sc-048), guides the crew through the wet-wall via earpiece (ev-024 sc-105), is shot and left for dead by Cypher then returns charred and bloody to kill him with a lightning bolt (ev-029 sc-137-141).

entity_roster.name: The Matrix
entity_roster.description: A computer-generated dreamworld of the world as it was [...], pulled over eyes as a prison for the mind to keep humans docile while converting them into coppertop batteries (ev-013 sc-039).

entity_roster.name: Hardline Phones
entity_roster.description: Copper-wired, ringing telephones — payphones, hotel room phones, the TV repair shop phone at Franklin and Erie — that are the only viable exits for a jacked-in mind; cutting the hardline springs the trap (ev-003 sc-005, ev-023 sc-085, ev-028 sc-130).

entity_roster.name: Pod Fields and Magenta Amnion
entity_roster.description: Endless towers of glowing petals holding humans floating in magenta gelatin, each wired via coaxial cable and cerebrum chip, where humans are grown not born after the sky was scorched (ev-011 sc-031-034, ev-013 sc-039).

entity_roster.name: Sentinels
entity_roster.description: Squid-like machines sweeping sewer mains that hunt the Nebuchadnezzar's electromagnetic wake, forcing the ship into a tiny supply line and to kill power and arm the EMP as its only weapon (ev-019 sc-066-072, ev-044 sc-209).

plot_briefs.name: Neo's Awakening — Becoming the One
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Neo wants to answer 'What is the Matrix?' and later to become the One Morpheus believes he is, because the question haunts him as a splinter and Morpheus frames it as enslavement (ev-010 sc-028).
plot_briefs.what_resists: The Agents who trace and possess anyone hardwired (ev-018 sc-065, ev-037 sc-176), the system's rule that the mind makes death real (ev-013 sc-039), and Neo's own disbelief that makes him fail the dojo and the jump (ev-015 sc-056, ev-016 sc-058).
plot_briefs.cost: He loses his job, his body and his world — mouth sealed and bugged (ev-007 sc-020), mirror consumed and pod severed (ev-011 sc-031), beaten and bloodied in training (ev-016 sc-061) — and must die from three chest shots before revival (ev-044 sc-209).
plot_briefs.resolution: Trinity's kiss restarts his flatlined monitors (ev-044 sc-211) and he halts bullets, reads the hall as code and bursts out of Smith, destroying the first Agent ever so the survivors feel fear (ev-045 sc-216-218), then escapes via ringing phone as Morpheus triggers the EMP (ev-046 sc-219-222).

plot_briefs.name: The Rescue of Morpheus
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Neo and Trinity want to pull Morpheus out alive after he is captured and doubled-serum tortured for Zion's mainframe codes (ev-031 sc-144-147), because Neo believes he can bring him back despite denying he is the One (ev-032 sc-148).
plot_briefs.what_resists: A heavily guarded government building, grenade launchers and Agents Brown, Jones and Smith who gun down the helicopter extraction, with Smith shooting Morpheus mid-dive (ev-033 sc-155, ev-034 sc-165-169).
plot_briefs.cost: They expend their arsenal, risk certain death re-entering a traced system, and Neo is left alone in the subway when Trinity is forced out a breath before Smith's bullet (ev-037 sc-176-178).
plot_briefs.resolution: Neo drops the helicopter onto the executive office, guns down the Agents, catches Morpheus's handcuffed wrist mid-fall and extracts him via climbing rope and rain gutter (ev-034 sc-165-169), securing an exit call for the rooftop (ev-035 sc-170-172).

plot_briefs.name: Cypher's Betrayal
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: Cypher wants to be reinserted into the Matrix as a wealthy, important actor who remembers nothing, because he recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count and finds real-world hardship unbearable (ev-020 sc-073-074).
plot_briefs.what_resists: The crew's trust and Tank's operator watch; Cypher must covertly drop a phone in the garbage can on the Oracle trip (ev-021 sc-075) and lie about an accident after shooting Tank (ev-029 sc-137).
plot_briefs.cost: He murders Apoc and Switch by yanking their plugs and delivers Morpheus to the Agents (ev-029 sc-137-141), and Dozer dies sizzling in his harness (ev-029 sc-139).
plot_briefs.resolution: Tank, left charred and bloody for dead, survives and levels a rifle to kill Cypher with a lightning bolt before Cypher can unplug Neo (ev-029 sc-141), saving Neo and Trinity who wake on the main deck (ev-030 sc-142-143).

plot_briefs.name: Crew Survival Against the Machines
plot_briefs.who_wants_what: The Nebuchadnezzar crew wants to stay alive in the real world while jacked-in teammates are vulnerable, because Sentinels hunt their electromagnetic wake (ev-019 sc-066).
plot_briefs.what_resists: Sentinels sweeping the sewer main that force the ship into a too-small supply line, requiring total power kill and silent running while the machine glides directly over them (ev-019 sc-066-072).
plot_briefs.cost: They must go cold and silent, arm the EMP as the only weapon, and cannot fire it until the jacked-in crew exits, leaving Morpheus weeping at the switch as Neo flatlines and sentinels breach the hull (ev-044 sc-209, ev-046 sc-219).
plot_briefs.resolution: At Trinity's 'Now!' timed to Neo's code-stream dive for the phone, Morpheus turns the key and the EMP's blinding white light drops the sentinels dead, allowing Neo to wake at Trinity's voice (ev-046 sc-219-222, ev-047 sc-223).

turning_points.name: Inciting Incident — Follow the White Rabbit
turning_points.where: Early Act One, ev-004 sc-012-013: Neo's PC types on its own and Trinity's white rabbit pin makes him break his plan to work and go out, committing to the hunt for Morpheus.

turning_points.name: Plot Point 1 — The Red Pill
turning_points.where: End of Act One, ev-010 sc-028-030: Morpheus offers blue pill (story ends) vs red pill (stay in Wonderland); Neo swallows red, the mirror liquefies and the trace locks, making return impossible.

turning_points.name: Midpoint — Desert of the Real and Failed Tests
turning_points.where: Mid Act Two, ev-013 sc-039-044 and ev-015-016 sc-048-062: Neo learns humans are farmed batteries and recoils, then is beaten in the dojo and falls short on the rooftop jump, proving belief not technique governs the system.

turning_points.name: Plot Point 2 — Oracle's Verdict and the Trap
turning_points.where: Late Act Two, ev-023 sc-085-104 and ev-025 sc-115-121: Oracle tells Neo he is not the One and one must die; deja-vu signals the Matrix was changed, hardline cut, Mouse killed, and Morpheus sacrifices himself to force Trinity to get Neo out.

turning_points.name: Climax — Death and Resurrection as the One
turning_points.where: Act Three, ev-043 sc-205-208 through ev-045 sc-216-218: Neo is shot three times in hall 303 and flatlines (ev-044 sc-209), Trinity's kiss revives him (ev-044 sc-211), he halts bullets and destroys Smith from inside, then escapes via ringing phone as EMP kills Sentinels (ev-046 sc-219).

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: Choose painful self-knowledge: swallow the red pill and stay in Wonderland to see the prison for your mind, even though the truth is that humans are farmed in magenta amnion (ev-010 sc-028, ev-013 sc-039).
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Choose blissful ignorance: take the blue pill and end the story, or trade betrayal for a steak that isn't real because 'ignorance is bliss' and you want to be rich and remember nothing (ev-010 sc-028, ev-020 sc-074).
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: Neo's choice versus Cypher's steak-deal with Smith; both are defensible because truth costs Neo his body and world (ev-011 sc-031) while illusion costs Cypher his crew and soul (ev-029 sc-137).

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: Preserve yourself: accept Morpheus is lost, pull his plug and escape while escape is possible, as the crew's survival protocol dictates (ev-032 sc-148).
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Sacrifice for another: re-enter the Matrix to pull Morpheus out alive even though everyone who has fought an Agent has died and Neo denies he is the One, so the gamble has no prophetic guarantee (ev-018 sc-065, ev-032 sc-148).
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: Morpheus pinning the Agent to let Trinity get Neo out (ev-025 sc-119) versus Neo stopping the plug pull to go back in (ev-032 sc-148); both horns cost lives priced in the story.

human_experience_dilemmas.side_a: Fate is written: the Oracle prophesied the One's return and tells Neo he is not the One yet and must choose which life to save (ev-014 sc-045, ev-023 sc-085), and Morpheus declares 'the search is over' (ev-014 sc-045).
human_experience_dilemmas.side_b: Choice overrides destiny: Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces by the third rail and hurls him into the tunnel ceiling (ev-039 sc-182), and later refuses death itself to become the One by acting as if he believes (ev-045 sc-216).
human_experience_dilemmas.anchored_in: Oracle's prophecy and Smith's pronouncement of inevitability versus Neo's subway refusal and resurrection; the story keeps both readings alive until the final code-vision.

state_dimensions: Awakening — asleep in simulation vs awake in the desert of the real (ev-010 red pill, ev-013 Construct)
Belief — doubt that makes rules real vs faith that bends/breaks them (ev-015 dojo, ev-016 jump, ev-045 bullet stop)
Control — enslaved battery under system control vs self-authored freedom (ev-013 fields, ev-020 Cypher's steak)
Identity — Thomas Anderson vs Neo vs the One (ev-007 two lives, ev-032 denial, ev-045 declaration)
constraints: Hardline exit discipline: every jack-in must have a pre-planned ringing phone and trace window; no wireless escapes (ev-003, ev-024, ev-028).
Lethality parity: any wound or death in the Matrix is real unless belief explicitly rewrites the rule, so training injuries and flatlines carry weight (ev-013, ev-016 sc-061, ev-044 sc-209).
Agent possession logic: any hardwired bystander can become an Agent instantly, so crowds are not cover but potential enemies (ev-018 sc-065, ev-037 sc-176).
keep_in_mind: Keep code visible as cascading green glyphs when Neo finally sees the Matrix as code (ev-045 sc-216); do not explain bending with dialogue alone.
Keep Agents as system programs in suits and sunglasses, not monsters; their horror is possession and inevitability (ev-018, ev-039).
Keep the real world tactile and rusted — magenta amnion, coaxial jacks, sewer mains and EMP key — to contrast the clean simulation (ev-011, ev-019, ev-046).
